Colour palettes

Source: vignettes/articles/palettes.Rmd
palettes.Rmd

bioToolkit has 41 palettes, taken from published sources and credited below. Every plot has one cols argument that takes a palette name, so this page is the menu: pick a palette by name, or pick colours from it by their index.

To Use
colour a plot with a palette cols = "okabe-ito"
reverse a palette add _r to its name: cols = "viridis_r"
take some colours, in your order bt_palette("scanpy-20")[c(1, 3, 2)] (indices as shown below)
get n colours bt_palette("seq-blue", n = 5) (qualitative palettes give their first n)
see palettes, or your own colours, in R show_palettes()
list names, types and sources list_palettes()
check colours for colour blindness check_palette()

Hover a swatch to see its index and hex code. Qualitative palettes are for groups (cell types, conditions); sequential palettes for values from low to high (expression, significance); diverging palettes for values on both sides of a centre (fold changes, z-scores, NES).

Defaults

The plots use these palettes when cols is not given:

Values Default Used by
Groups, up to 20 scanpy-20 every plot coloured by group
Groups, 21 to 102 scanpy-102 every plot coloured by group
Expression on an embedding plasma_r FeaturePlot_bioToolkit()
Mean expression, not scaled viridis_r DotPlot_bioToolkit()
Mean expression, not scaled, heatmap magma DoHeatmap_bioToolkit()
Significance, one-directional values seq-purple, seq-blue, … enrichment plots (one hue per panel), plot_pca(), plot_variance_explained()
Signed values (z-scores, fold changes, NES) blue-magenta dot plots, DE plots, enrichment NES, density differences, diverging feature plots
z-scores of single cells teal-yellow DoHeatmap_bioToolkit()

Qualitative

For groups. They are never interpolated: a colour in between two group colours would read as an intermediate group, so bt_palette(name, n) stops when a palette has fewer than n colours.

Sequential

For values from low to high. The seq-* palettes are single-hue ramps trimmed to the same lightness range (CIE L* 80 to 30): not so pale that low values vanish on white, not so dark that the hue is lost, and the same value has the same lightness whatever the hue, so that panels in different hues stay comparable.

Diverging

For values on both sides of a centre, drawn in the middle colour. The plots put the centre at 0 and stretch each side to its own end (see Colours). Index 1 is the low end; for a scale of your own, the low, middle and high colours are e.g. bt_palette("tol-burd")[c(1, 5, 9)].

Your own colours

show_palettes() draws palettes by name, a vector of your own colours, or a list of both, with the index of each colour. For example, colours picked for cell types next to the palette they came from:

cell_cols <- bt_palette("scanpy-20")[c(1, 2, 3, 5, 4)]
names(cell_cols) <- c("CD4 T", "CD14 Mono", "B", "CD8 T", "NK")

show_palettes(list(
    "cell types" = cell_cols,
    "scanpy-20",
    warm = c("gold", "darkorange", "firebrick")
))

Name the colours by group and pass them as cols, so that each cell type keeps its colour in every figure; check_palette(cell_cols) flags pairs that become hard to tell apart with colour blindness (see Colour vision deficiency).

Adding a palette

New palettes come from a citable source, with hex values copied from it (or from a package that reproduces it), never retyped from memory. Each is an entry of palette_list() in R/palettes.R, with its colours, type and source; the package tests check every entry.
